physical_harm: The deceased suffered multiple wounds, disfigured face, pulverized bones, and brain matter flowing out from wounds, indicating fatal injury.
number_of_offences: The appellant was charged with one offence under Section 302, and it was upheld by the courts.
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused acted with intention to cause death, indicating premeditation.
motive: Previous enmity between the accused and the deceased
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of witnesses with regard to earlier incident of altercation between deceased and the accused-appellant furnishing motive to the accused - There was previous enmity - Evidence of eye witnesses supporting the prosecution case and found reliable - The nature of injuries on the deceased suggested intention to cause death or fatal injury on the vital part of the body with full force sufficient to cause death.
witness_credibility: Both the courts below found the evidence of PW 3 and PW 4 to be reliable. Evidence of PW 7 widow of the deceased was also believed with regard to the earlier incident furnishing motive to the accused. PW 2 also corroborated the version given by the eye witnesses. The defence version of the accused was not found to be reliable.

legal_representation.accused: Hema Sahu, Rajendra Sahu, C. L. Sahu

investigation_status: FIR registered, post mortem conducted, investigation completed, accused sent up for trial
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused-appellant was responsible for causing the death of the deceased, supported by reliable evidence of witnesses, including PW 3 and PW 4, and PW 7's account of the earlier incident furnishing motive. The evidence indicated prior enmity and that the injuries on the deceased suggested intention to cause death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the case fell under Exception 4 to Section 300 of the Penal Code, as it was a case of sudden fight, and that the injuries on the accused indicated a free fight. They also claimed the accused was falsely implicated.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the determination of whether a case falls under Section 302 or 304 of the Penal Code depends on various factors, including the nature of the weapon, the circumstances of the incident, and whether the attack was in the heat of passion or with prior enmity.
precedent_relied_upon: Ankush Shivaji Gaikwad vs. State of Maharashtra 2013 (8) SCR 863
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the accused was found responsible for causing the death of the deceased, with the injuries indicating intention to cause death or a fatal injury, and there was no evidence of free fight or sudden provocation.
judicial_aggravating_factors: Prior enmity, the nature of injuries on the deceased suggesting intention to cause death, and the accused acting in a cruel manner.
